questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An International Qualified Nurse (IQN) has recently commenced employment in an Australian hospital. During a busy shift, the registered nurse asks the IQN to administer intravenous antibiotics independently. Although the IQN performed this procedure frequently in their home country, they have not yet completed the hospital's competency assessment. What is the MOST appropriate action?

options.text: Ask another nurse to sign the medication chart afterwards.
Decline to care for the patient.
Administer the medication because of previous experience.
Complete the medication administration under supervision after informing the RN of the competency limitation.

questions.rationale: Professional nurses must work within both their professional scope of practice and organisational policies. Previous overseas experience does not replace local competency requirements. Seeking supervision protects patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is caring for four patients. Which patient should be assessed FIRST?

options.text: A patient complaining of sudden difficulty breathing.
A patient requesting assistance with breakfast.
A patient asking when the doctor will visit.
A patient requesting pain medication for chronic arthritis.

questions.rationale: Airway and breathing always take priority. Sudden shortness of breath may indicate rapid clinical deterioration requiring immediate assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An IQN notices that another nurse is preparing medication for the wrong patient. What should the IQN do?

options.text: Report the incident after the shift.
Immediately intervene respectfully to prevent the error.

questions.rationale: Patient safety is everyone's responsibility. Immediate intervention prevents harm while maintaining professional communication.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient asks the nurse, "I don't understand why I'm having this treatment." What is the BEST nursing response?

options.text: Explain the treatment within your scope of practice and clarify any concerns.
Tell the patient not to worry.

questions.rationale: Nurses play an important role in patient education and informed decision-making within their professional scope.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: During handover, a nurse receives information that one patient has deteriorated overnight. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Visit the deteriorating patient immediately after reviewing the handover.
Read all patient notes before assessment.

questions.rationale: Patients showing signs of deterioration require timely assessment before routine care activities.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse receives a verbal medication order over the telephone. Which action is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Ask another nurse to remember it.
Repeat the order back to confirm accuracy and follow organisational policy.

questions.rationale: Read-back confirmation reduces communication errors and supports medication safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An elderly patient repeatedly attempts to get out of bed despite being identified as a high falls risk. What is the nurse's BEST intervention?

options.text: Increase observation, address the reason for getting up, and implement falls prevention strategies.
Tell the patient to stay in bed.

questions.rationale: The nurse should first identify and address underlying needs while implementing evidence-based falls prevention measures. Restraints should not be used routinely.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An IQN notices that a colleague frequently omits hand hygiene between patients. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Tell patients to remind the colleague.
Discuss the issue respectfully with the colleague and escalate if necessary.

questions.rationale: Professional accountability includes addressing unsafe practice respectfully while promoting patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient refuses a blood transfusion because of religious beliefs. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Respect the patient's decision, ensure the healthcare team is informed, and document appropriately.
Ask the family to persuade the patient.
Convince the patient to accept treatment.

questions.rationale: Competent adults have the legal right to refuse treatment, even when refusal may affect their health.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action best demonstrates culturally safe nursing practice?

options.text: Asking each patient about individual beliefs, preferences, and healthcare expectations.
Assuming all patients from one culture have identical beliefs.

questions.rationale: Cultural safety requires recognising every patient's individual values rather than relying on stereotypes.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient suddenly becomes confused after surgery. What is the nurse's PRIORITY action?

options.text: Ask family members if this is normal.
Perform an immediate assessment and notify the appropriate clinician.

questions.rationale: Acute confusion may indicate delirium or other serious complications requiring prompt assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices that an intravenous infusion pump is alarming continuously. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Silence the alarm and continue other work.
Assess the patient and identify the cause of the alarm.

questions.rationale: Patient assessment always takes priority when medical equipment alarms.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient expresses dissatisfaction with their care. What is the MOST professional nursing response?

options.text: Listen actively, acknowledge concerns, and attempt to resolve the issue appropriately.
Tell the patient to speak only with the doctor.

questions.rationale: Professional communication involves active listening, empathy, and timely resolution of patient concerns.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which patient should the nurse review FIRST?

options.text: Patient with new onset chest pain.

questions.rationale: Chest pain may indicate a life-threatening cardiac event requiring immediate assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An IQN is unfamiliar with a local hospital policy. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Ask another nurse to complete the task permanently.

questions.rationale: Understanding local organisational policies is essential for safe and compliant nursing practice.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient begins to deteriorate rapidly. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Wait for the doctor to arrive.
Activate the appropriate clinical escalation process according to hospital policy.

questions.rationale: Early recognition and escalation of clinical deterioration improve patient outcomes.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which behaviour best demonstrates professional resilience?

options.text: Reflecting on practice and learning from experience.

questions.rationale: Reflective practice promotes continuous professional development and improves future clinical performance.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A family member asks the nurse for confidential information about another patient in the same room. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Confidentiality remains a legal and ethical obligation regardless of who requests the information.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse identifies a potential medication error before it reaches the patient. What should happen NEXT?

options.text: Ignore it because no harm occurred.
Report the near miss according to organisational policy.

questions.rationale: Reporting near misses supports organisational learning and strengthens patient safety systems.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects the role of an International Qualified Nurse transitioning into a new healthcare system?

options.text: Previous experience removes the need to learn local practice.
Successful transition requires adapting to local legislation, standards, communication practices, and organisational policies while building on previous professional experience.
International nurses should avoid asking questions.

questions.rationale: Transitioning to international practice involves integrating previous experience with the legal, professional, ethical, and cultural expectations of the new healthcare system. This supports safe, effective, and patient-centred care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse begins a shift caring for four patients. Which patient should be assessed FIRST?

options.text: A patient waiting for routine wound dressing.
A patient requesting assistance with breakfast.
A patient reporting sudden onset chest pain and shortness of breath.

questions.rationale: Clinical reasoning begins with prioritising life-threatening conditions. Chest pain with shortness of breath may indicate acute coronary syndrome or pulmonary embolism requiring immediate assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A postoperative patient suddenly becomes restless, anxious and complains of difficulty breathing. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Assess airway, breathing and oxygen saturation immediately.

questions.rationale: Restlessness and dyspnoea are early indicators of patient deterioration. Immediate ABC assessment is the priority.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient's blood pressure has decreased from 128/78 mmHg to 88/54 mmHg within one hour following surgery. What is the nurse's PRIORITY action?

options.text: Assess the patient immediately and escalate according to hospital policy.
Wait until the doctor arrives on the ward.

questions.rationale: A significant drop in blood pressure may indicate haemorrhage or shock. Early recognition and escalation improve patient outcomes.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient receiving oxygen therapy has an oxygen saturation of 84% despite oxygen being in place. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Assess the patient and ensure the oxygen equipment is functioning correctly while initiating appropriate escalation.

questions.rationale: Low oxygen saturation requires immediate assessment of both the patient and the oxygen delivery system before further interventions.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Evidence-based nursing practice is best described as:

options.text: Combining research evidence, clinical expertise and patient preferences.

questions.rationale: Evidence-based practice integrates current research, professional expertise and the patient's values to provide optimal care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices a patient's respiratory rate has increased from 18 to 30 breaths per minute over two hours. What should the nurse recognise?

options.text: Repeat observations at the end of the shift.
Respiratory rate is often an early indicator of clinical deterioration.
Respiratory rate is less important than pulse rate.

questions.rationale: An increasing respiratory rate is one of the earliest indicators of serious patient deterioration.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient develops confusion, fever and low blood pressure. Which condition should the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Confusion, fever and hypotension are classic warning signs of sepsis requiring immediate intervention.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient says, "I don't think this medication is working." What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: Assess the patient's symptoms and evaluate the effectiveness of the treatment.

questions.rationale: Clinical reasoning requires nurses to evaluate treatment effectiveness based on patient assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which patient requires the MOST urgent review?

options.text: New confusion with oxygen saturation of 88%.

questions.rationale: Acute confusion and hypoxaemia suggest serious deterioration requiring immediate assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices that a patient's urine output has fallen significantly over the previous four hours. Why is this concerning?

options.text: Patients normally produce little urine after surgery.
It is expected in all patients.
It may indicate impaired kidney perfusion or deterioration.

questions.rationale: Reduced urine output is an important clinical indicator of reduced organ perfusion and possible deterioration.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When reviewing patient observations, which trend is MOST important?

options.text: The overall pattern of changing observations over time.

questions.rationale: Clinical reasoning involves recognising trends rather than relying on isolated measurements.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient complains of increasing pain despite receiving analgesia. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Tell the patient pain is expected.
Wait until the next medication round.
Reassess the patient and investigate possible causes.

questions.rationale: Persistent pain may indicate complications and requires reassessment rather than assumptions.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse identifies that current evidence recommends a different wound dressing than the one routinely used. What is the BEST action?

options.text: Discuss the evidence with the clinical team following organisational procedures.

questions.rationale: Evidence-based improvements should be introduced collaboratively and within organisational governance.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient suddenly becomes pale, sweaty and dizzy after standing. What is the nurse's FIRST action?

options.text: Encourage the patient to continue walking.
Assist the patient back to a safe position and assess vital signs.

questions.rationale: Immediate patient safety and assessment are priorities when signs of instability occur.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which assessment finding requires immediate escalation?

options.text: New onset reduced level of consciousness.

questions.rationale: Altered consciousness is a major sign of clinical deterioration requiring urgent review.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects clinical reasoning?

options.text: Waiting for doctors before assessing patients.
Collecting assessment data, interpreting findings and making safe clinical decisions.

questions.rationale: Clinical reasoning is a structured thinking process used to deliver safe, evidence-based care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient with diabetes becomes sweaty, confused and shaky before lunch. What should the nurse suspect FIRST?
questions.rationale: These are classic symptoms of low blood glucose requiring immediate assessment and management.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient's family expresses concern that "something isn't right." What should the nurse do?

options.text: Tell them to wait for the doctor.
Take the concern seriously and reassess the patient.

questions.rationale: Family members often recognise subtle changes before clinical deterioration becomes obvious.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which nursing action demonstrates evidence-based medication safety?

options.text: Delegating medication administration to untrained staff.
Following current medication administration guidelines and verifying patient identity.

questions.rationale: Evidence-based medication practices reduce medication errors and improve patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse has assessed a deteriorating patient, initiated immediate nursing interventions, and activated the hospital's escalation process. What should the nurse do NEXT?

options.text: Continue monitoring, communicate clearly with the responding team, and document all assessments and interventions.

questions.rationale: Clinical reasoning continues after escalation. Ongoing assessment, effective communication, and accurate documentation are essential for safe patient management.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: During shift handover, the outgoing nurse reports that a patient "looks unwell" but provides no further details. What should the receiving nurse do?

options.text: Request specific clinical information, including observations, recent changes, and interventions.
Accept the handover and continue the shift.
Wait until the doctor reviews the patient.

questions.rationale: Effective handover requires clear, structured, and objective information to ensure continuity and patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is documenting a patient's wound assessment. Which documentation is MOST appropriate?

options.text: "Surgical wound measures 4 cm × 2 cm with minimal serous drainage. Surrounding skin intact. Patient reports pain score 3/10."

questions.rationale: Documentation should be objective, accurate, measurable, and free from personal opinions.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient suddenly becomes hypotensive. After initiating emergency interventions, what documentation is MOST important?

options.text: A brief summary at the end of the shift.
Assessments, interventions, patient responses, notifications, and time of events.

questions.rationale: Comprehensive documentation provides a legal record and ensures continuity of care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient speaks very little English and requires consent for a procedure. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Qualified interpreters ensure informed consent, patient safety, and legal compliance.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient tells the nurse, "Please don't tell my family about my diagnosis." What is the MOST appropriate response?

options.text: Tell the family after the shift.
Ask another nurse to tell them.
Respect the patient's wishes unless disclosure is legally required.

questions.rationale: Patients have the right to confidentiality and control over disclosure of personal health information.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which communication technique best demonstrates active listening?

options.text: Looking at the computer while the patient speaks.
Maintaining eye contact, summarising the patient's concerns, and asking clarifying questions.

questions.rationale: Active listening promotes understanding, trust, and therapeutic relationships.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse receives a telephone order from a doctor. Which action is safest?

options.text: Write it down and administer immediately.
Read the order back to confirm accuracy before implementation.

questions.rationale: Read-back communication significantly reduces medication and communication errors.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient becomes angry after waiting several hours for diagnostic tests. What is the BEST nursing response?

options.text: Tell the patient to calm down.
Listen to the patient's concerns, acknowledge the frustration, explain the situation honestly, and update them on the plan.

questions.rationale: Acknowledging emotions and providing clear information helps de-escalate conflict.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A colleague asks you to document observations that they performed. What should you do?

options.text: Explain that documentation should only reflect care you personally provided or observed.

questions.rationale: Professional documentation must accurately reflect the nurse's own actions and observations.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects professional communication?

options.text: Clear, respectful, timely, accurate, and patient-centred communication.

questions.rationale: Professional communication improves teamwork and patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient begins crying while discussing a recent cancer diagnosis. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Sit quietly, acknowledge the patient's emotions, and encourage them to express their feelings.
Offer reassurance by saying "Everything will be fine."

questions.rationale: Therapeutic communication supports emotional wellbeing through empathy and active listening.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices incorrect information documented in the patient's notes by another clinician. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Follow organisational procedures to report and correct the documentation.

questions.rationale: Errors should be corrected according to legal and organisational documentation standards.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement about electronic health records (EHRs) is correct?

options.text: Family members may access records without permission.
Only authorised healthcare professionals should access patient records.
Passwords may be shared with colleagues.
Records may be viewed out of curiosity.

questions.rationale: Electronic health records are confidential legal documents with controlled access.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is giving a clinical handover using the ISBAR framework. What does the letter "A" represent?
questions.rationale: ISBAR stands for Identification, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient refuses medication but appears fully competent to make decisions. What should the nurse document?

options.text: The medication refusal, education provided, patient's stated reason, and healthcare team notification.

questions.rationale: Documentation should accurately record informed refusal and subsequent nursing actions.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A family member asks, "Can you tell me the results of my father's tests?" The patient has not given permission to share information. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Politely explain that patient consent is required before discussing confidential information.

questions.rationale: Confidentiality remains a professional and legal responsibility.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse realises they documented medication administration before actually giving the medication. What is the MOST appropriate action?

options.text: Administer the medication later without changing documentation.
Correct the documentation according to organisational policy and ensure the medication is administered safely.

questions.rationale: Documentation should always reflect actual care provided. Errors must be corrected transparently.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient with hearing impairment struggles to understand discharge instructions. What is the BEST nursing intervention?

options.text: Give instructions to a visitor instead.
Provide written information, face the patient while speaking, and confirm understanding.

questions.rationale: Communication should be adapted to meet individual patient needs while confirming understanding.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes therapeutic communication?

options.text: Building trust through empathy, respect, active listening, and patient-centred responses.
Giving advice based on personal opinion.

questions.rationale: Therapeutic communication supports patient engagement, emotional wellbeing, and quality care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: During handover, the nurse notices that an important allergy was omitted from the report. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Clarify the allergy immediately, update the receiving team, and ensure documentation is accurate.

questions.rationale: Accurate communication during clinical handover is essential for preventing medication errors and protecting patient safety.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient newly diagnosed with diabetes says, "My life is over." What is the MOST appropriate nursing response?

options.text: "Many people live well with diabetes. Tell me what worries you the most."

questions.rationale: Acknowledging emotions and inviting discussion demonstrates empathy and supports person-centred care.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An elderly patient refuses assistance with showering. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Explore the patient's concerns while respecting dignity and promoting independence.

questions.rationale: Person-centred care respects patient autonomy while exploring barriers and encouraging participation.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient from a different cultural background refuses certain foods served in hospital. What is the nurse's BEST action?

options.text: Ask family to bring food without consultation.
Tell the patient nutrition is more important than culture.
Explain hospital meals cannot be changed.
Explore dietary preferences and arrange appropriate alternatives where possible.

questions.rationale: Culturally safe nursing respects dietary beliefs while maintaining nutritional requirements.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient with dementia becomes agitated during personal care. What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: Complete the task quickly despite resistance.
Speak calmly, explain each step, and allow additional time for reassurance.

questions.rationale: Patients with cognitive impairment respond better to calm communication, reassurance, and familiar routines.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient nearing end of life says, "I'm frightened about what will happen." What is the MOST therapeutic nursing response?

options.text: "Can you tell me what concerns you most?"

questions.rationale: Open-ended questions encourage expression of fears and allow nurses to provide emotional support.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices that a patient's pain has increased despite regular analgesia. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Reassess the pain, investigate contributing factors, and discuss additional management with the healthcare team.
Wait until the next medication round.

questions.rationale: Pain assessment is continuous and requires evaluation of treatment effectiveness.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient's family requests to remain present during clinical discussions. The patient agrees. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Include the family while ensuring the patient's wishes remain central.

questions.rationale: Family-centred care supports patient preferences while maintaining patient autonomy.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient becomes angry after waiting several hours for surgery. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Listen to the patient's concerns, acknowledge frustration, explain the reason for the delay, and provide updates.
Tell the patient delays are common.

questions.rationale: Acknowledging emotions and providing honest information helps reduce anxiety and builds trust.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient requests information from the internet regarding a new treatment. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Tell the patient not to use the internet.
Discuss reliable evidence-based resources and encourage questions.

questions.rationale: Supporting health literacy enables patients to participate in informed healthcare decisions.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient with limited mobility wishes to dress independently. What is the BEST nursing approach?

options.text: Ask the family to dress the patient.
Complete the task without involving the patient.
Encourage the patient to perform as much as safely possible while providing assistance only when required.

questions.rationale: Promoting independence maintains function, dignity, and confidence.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which nursing action best demonstrates compassion?

options.text: Recognising emotional needs while providing respectful care.

questions.rationale: Compassion combines empathy with meaningful actions that address the patient's physical and emotional wellbeing.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient expresses concern about returning home after discharge. What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: Refer the patient to another ward.
Assess discharge needs and collaborate with the multidisciplinary team to plan ongoing support.
Tell the patient everything will be fine.

questions.rationale: Safe discharge planning begins early and involves coordinated care.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient receiving palliative care refuses further treatment. What principle should guide the nurse?

options.text: Convince the patient to continue treatment.
Respect informed decisions while providing compassionate support.

questions.rationale: Competent patients have the right to make informed healthcare decisions.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices a patient becoming withdrawn and unusually quiet. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Assess emotional wellbeing and encourage discussion in a supportive environment.

questions.rationale: Changes in behaviour may indicate anxiety, depression, or other concerns requiring assessment.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient has difficulty understanding discharge medications. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Give the information only to family.
Use plain language, written information, and ask the patient to explain the instructions back.

questions.rationale: The teach-back method confirms understanding and promotes safe self-management.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient asks for a second opinion regarding treatment options. What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: Support the patient's right to seek further medical advice.
Tell the patient it is unnecessary.

questions.rationale: Patients have the right to participate fully in decisions regarding their healthcare.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient becomes upset after receiving unexpected test results. What should the nurse prioritise?

options.text: Providing emotional support, assessing immediate needs, and facilitating appropriate follow-up.
Asking another patient to comfort them.

questions.rationale: Emotional support is an essential component of holistic nursing care.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient asks, "How can I prevent this illness from happening again?" What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: Tell the patient not to worry.
Explain evidence-based health promotion strategies relevant to the patient's condition.

questions.rationale: Health promotion and patient education are key nursing responsibilities.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A multidisciplinary team is planning a patient's discharge. What is the nurse's PRIMARY role?

options.text: Allow others to make all decisions.
Advocate for the patient's needs while coordinating communication between the patient, family, and healthcare team.

questions.rationale: Nurses play a central role in coordinating safe, person-centred discharge planning.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement BEST reflects person-centred nursing practice?

options.text: The healthcare team makes decisions on behalf of the patient.
Care is planned around the patient's values, preferences, goals, and active participation while ensuring safety and evidence-based practice.
All patients receive identical care regardless of individual needs.
Nursing focuses only on physical illness.

questions.rationale: Person-centred nursing recognises each patient as a unique individual and integrates clinical expertise, evidence, compassion, and shared decision-making to deliver holistic, high-quality care.
